extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and examiners working on AI/software-related patent filings in JPO and CNIPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and comparative examination practice for drafting and prosecuting AI- and software-related patent applications before the Japan Patent Office (JPO) and the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA). Focuses on eligibility, claim drafting, clarity, enablement, and inventive_step considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim title clarity (product vs process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The titles of the subject matter of claims 'data', 'computer program' and 'model' do not indicate clearly whether the claims are product claims or process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNIPA requires the type of each claim to be clear; titles of AI-related claims may be drafted as 'A method for ……', 'A system for ……', 'A computer apparatus' or 'A computer-readable storage medium'. Where titles like 'data', 'computer program' or 'model' are ambiguous, applicants should modify the title (e.g. 'A Method for training model', 'A model training system/apparatus') to indicate product or process and thereby clarify the extent of protection (Article 26.4 CPL).

rubrics_metrics.name: JPO eligibility disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who intends to file a software-related invention with the JPO is required to explicitly disclose the invention as 'the creation of technical ideas utilizing the laws of nature' or 'information processing by the software realized using hardware resources concretely', which is utilizing the laws of nature as a whole to satisfy the requirement for eligibility in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting specification and claims for filings at the JPO, explicitly describe how the software produces technical effects and how software processing concretely uses hardware resources (CPU, memory, etc.) so the claimed subject-matter is recognized as an 'invention' rather than mere information or abstract software.

rubrics_metrics.name: CNIPA eligibility disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the CNIPA, the applicant who intends to file an AI-related invention is required to explicitly disclose the invention as 'an aggregation of technical means applying the laws of nature to solve a technical problem'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the specification to show aggregation of technical means, the technical problem solved, and the technical effect obtained. This framing supports treating AI-related solutions as technical solutions under Article 2.2 of Chinese Patent Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible subject-matter wording for software-related filings (JPO practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a 'program,' 'data structure,' or 'model,' etc., as a subject matter in the category of an 'invention of a product.' If the subject matter of the claim is a 'program', the category of invention is clearly recognized as an 'invention of a product'. If a 'data structure' or 'model' is recognized as equivalent to a computer program, the category is allowed as an 'invention of a product'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wording in the claims and description that ties program/data/model to concrete software modules and hardware implementation to increase recognition as product-type inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere presentation of information is not an invention (JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere presentation of information (where the feature resides solely in the content of the information, and the main object is to present information) does not fall under 'invention' (creation of the technical idea utilizing a law of nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that only define the content of data (e.g., 'sugar content data of preharvest apples on trees') without specifying means or methods for presenting or technically obtaining that information will be treated as non-inventions. To overcome refusal, include technical means/measurement methods or processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical character via software–hardware cooperation (JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: If specific calculation or processing of specific information depending on intended use is implemented by specific means or procedures on which software and hardware resources co-operate (i.e., information processing by software realized using hardware resources concretely), then it is a creation of a technical idea utilizing a law of nature and falls under 'invention'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate in the description that claimed software constructs a specific information-processing system through cooperation of software and hardware (examples: CPU operations in accordance with stored trained weights causing specific calculations). Such concrete implementation supports eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical solution / technical effect requirement (CNIPA — Article 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution must solve a technical problem, utilize technical means, and obtain a technical effect. If so, it is the technical solution as provided for in Article 2.2 Chinese Patent Law and constitutes patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the specification and claims, identify the technical problem, explain how the invention uses technical means (e.g., measurement devices, algorithms producing technical processing of data), and describe the technical effect (e.g., enabling accurate analysis or measurement). CNIPA examples: trained model and sensor-measured data considered technical for these reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement / sufficiency of disclosure and claims supported by the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be enabled and supported by the description (sufficiency of disclosure / claims supported by the description). The comparative tables show JPO and CNIPA acceptances/refusals (O/X) based on these criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the specification contains sufficient detail to carry out the claimed invention and that claim scope is supported by the description. The examination may refuse claims lacking enablement or lacking support by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step assessment scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing inventive step, it is necessary to take the entire state of the art into consideration, but in the comparative study inventive step was assessed only working from the matter described under the heading 'State of the art (prior art, well-known art, etc.)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, examiners consider the whole prior art; applicants should prepare arguments and disclosures addressing relevant prior art and explain how claimed features provide a non-obvious technical contribution over it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting options for AI-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filed claims can be written as a process claim (a method for …), a product claim (a system for…, an apparatus for…), a computer-readable storage medium, or a computer program product; the claim category affects eligibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider drafting parallel claims in different categories (method, system/apparatus, computer program, storage medium) and use language that ties the claimed subject-matter to technical means and effects to improve chances at different offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data derived from technical measurement may be technical (CNIPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If data is produced by technical measurement (e.g., sugar content data measured by a portable near-infrared spectroscopic sensor), the data and related claims can be considered to have technical features and may constitute patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting patentability of 'data'-type claims, emphasize how the data is acquired via technical means and how the data is used in technical processing, showing technical effect and solution to a technical problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for clarity refusals (title and claim amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can modify the title of the subject matter to make claim type clear, e.g., change 'A trained model' or 'A computer program' to 'A Method for training model', 'A model training system/apparatus', etc., to comply with clarity provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend claim titles and claim preambles to explicitly indicate whether the claim is for a product, process, apparatus or storage medium to address Article 26.4 clarity objections at CNIPA (and similar clarity expectations at other offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standard reference (JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether inventions (e.g., Claim 3 in Case A-2) fall under 'invention' is judged in accordance with 'Examination Guidelines Part III, Chapter 1: Eligibility of Invention and Industrial Applicability' and thus is not examined from the viewpoint of the computer software per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on the cited examination guidelines when preparing arguments and amendments; craft descriptions to meet the guideline criteria for technical character and industrial applicability rather than attempting to argue solely on software-abstractness grounds.
